summary: Hyperion was tasked with a major refactoring of the `reality-merge` repository to clean up the root directory by moving several files and directories into a `gitignore/` directory. The agent also began the process of moving media files to new type-specific directories and updating markdown links. The session ended prematurely due to a series of API errors after encountering difficulties with file and directory manipulation.

tasks.name: Refactor `reality-merge` repository
tasks.description: Moved several directories (`chat/`, `inbox/`, `shared/`, `notion/`, `client_secret.json`, `token.json`, etc.) into a new `gitignore/` directory. Began moving media files and updating markdown links. The refactoring was complex and resulted in a corrupted state of the repository.

learnings.name: Handling complex file system operations
learnings.description: Complex, multi-step file system operations are prone to errors, especially when dealing with nested Git repositories and user interruptions. A more robust error handling and state management strategy is needed for such tasks.

learnings.name: API Error Recovery
learnings.description: The agent was unable to recover from a series of API errors, which ultimately led to the session's termination. The agent needs to be more resilient to API failures and have better recovery mechanisms.

conclusion: Hyperion's session was cut short by a series of errors during a complex refactoring task. While the agent made some progress, it left the repository in an inconsistent state that requires manual intervention to fix. This session highlights the need for more robust error handling and a more cautious approach to complex file system operations.
